newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: New Lithuanian PM aims for budget next month.
newsitem.headline: New Lithuanian PM aims for budget next month.

text.p: Lithuania's newly nominated Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius promised to present a new 1997 budget in December and name his new government within 10 days.
Vagnorius, one of the leaders of the right-wing Homeland Union party, was given the task of forming the government by President Algirdas Brazauskas.
The Homeland Union won 70 seats in the 141-seat parliament in recent elections and is to form a coalition government.
"The draft project of the budget should be submitted before December 15," Vagnorius told parliament after his nomination.

The outgoing Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP), which lost an election earlier this month, had drafted a budget envisaging a deficit of 596 million litas or 1.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). But the fate of the draft was not clear under the new government.
Vagnorius' nomination by Brazauskas has to be formally approved by parliament and then he will present his government within around 10 days.

Vagnorius also said his government would welcome foreign investment. Lithuania is viewed as the laggard of the Baltic states in terms of reform and few large and attractive companies have been put on the block.
"We are ready to give the green light to capital investment and to remove all the obstacles," he said.
He said he also wanted to boost exports to a level equal to around 55 percent to 60 percent of GDP.
Vagnorius also pledged to boost the average salary and pensions.
